caption:
Speed-to-lead research keeps landing on the same pattern.

Teams that automate the first reply answer new leads inside 15 minutes far more often than teams relying on manual follow-up.

The pattern holds across home services, legal and healthcare.

Here's why it matters: most leads contact two or three competitors at once. Whoever replies first usually books the job.

Pull your last 10 leads this week. Check the gap between when they came in and when someone replied.

If most sit past 15 minutes, build a reply that fires the instant the lead lands, then have a person follow up right behind it.

DM TRIAL

#SpeedToLead #ServiceBusiness #LeadFollowUp #HomeServices #SmallBusinessGrowth
rationale: Carousels remain the strongest format for depth and saves. The speed-to-lead gap between automated and manual responders is a well-documented industry pattern; reframing it as an honest general finding (rather than a single unverifiable report) keeps the post credible while still converting directly into a self-audit tactic and trial CTA.
